content: Crotamiton is a pesticide approved by the FDA for the treatment of scabies (caused by Sarcoptes scabiei) and for the symptomatic relief of pruritic skin conditions. Common adverse reactions include dermatitis and skin irritation. Adult Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Adults): Crotamiton is used for the eradication of scabies and for symptomatic treatment of pruritic skin. Application Instructions: Massage the medication gently into the affected areas until it is completely absorbed. Repeat as needed. For lotion formulations, shake well before use. For scabies, thoroughly massage the medication into the skin of the entire body from the chin down, paying special attention to folds and creases. A second application is recommended 24 hours later. Clothing and bed linens should be changed the next morning. A cleansing bath should be taken 48 hours after the last application. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adults): There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported use of crotamiton in adults. Pediatric Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Pediatrics): Limited information is available regarding FDA-labeled indications and dosage for pediatric patients. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Pediatrics): There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of crotamiton in pediatric patients. Contraindications Crotamiton (Eurax) should not be applied to patients who are sensitive or allergic to it or who exhibit primary irritation responses to topical medications. Warnings If severe irritation or sensitization occurs, discontinue treatment immediately and initiate appropriate therapy. Precautions Avoid applying Eurax to the eyes or mouth, as it may cause irritation. Do not apply to acutely inflamed skin or raw/weeping surfaces until the acute inflammation has subsided. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience: Primary irritation reactions, such as dermatitis, pruritus, and rash, as well as allergic sensitivity reactions, have been reported in some patients. Postmarketing Experience: Limited information is available regarding postmarketing experience with crotamiton. Drug Interactions No known drug interactions have been identified. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: FDA Pregnancy Category C: Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with Eurax. It is unknown whether Eurax can cause fetal harm when applied topically to a pregnant woman or affect reproductive capacity. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) guidance is not available for use in pregnant women. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available on the use of crotamiton during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: No FDA guidance is available regarding the use of crotamiton in nursing mothers. Pediatric Use: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established. Geriatric Use: Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 years and older to determine whether they respond differently than younger subjects. However, greater sensitivity in some older individuals cannot be ruled out. Gender, Race, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment, and Immunocompromised Patients: No specific FDA guidance is available for these populations. Administration and Monitoring Administration: For scabies: Massage thoroughly into the skin of the entire body from the chin down, paying attention to folds and creases. A second application is recommended 24 hours later. Change clothing and bed linens the next day. Contaminated items should be dry-cleaned or washed in the hot cycle of a washing machine. Take a cleansing bath 48 hours after the last application. For pruritus: Massage gently into affected areas until completely absorbed. Repeat as needed. Shake lotion well before use. Patient Directions for Scabies: Take a routine bath or shower. Massage Eurax cream or lotion into the skin from the chin to the toes, including folds and creases. Apply under fingernails after trimming them short, as scabies mites may remain there. A toothbrush can be used to apply the medication under the nails, but the toothbrush should be discarded immediately after use to avoid poisoning if reused in the mouth. A second application is recommended 24 hours later. A 60-gram tube or bottle is sufficient for two applications. Change clothing and bed linens the next day. Contaminated items may be dry-cleaned or washed in the hot cycle of a washing machine. Take a cleansing bath 48 hours after the last application. Monitoring: Limited information is available regarding monitoring of crotamiton. Overdosage There is no specific information on the effects of overtreatment with repeated topical applications in humans. A death was reported, but the cause was not confirmed. Accidental oral ingestion may cause a burning sensation in the mouth, irritation of the buccal, esophageal, and gastric mucosa, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. If accidental ingestion occurs, contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Pharmacology Mechanism of Action: Eurax exhibits scabicidal and antipruritic actions, though the mechanisms of these actions are not well understood. Structure: Eurax contains 10% (w/w) crotamiton USP in a vanishing-cream or emollient-lotion base. The cream also contains additional ingredients such as carbomer-934, cetyl alcohol, dimethicone, and others. Crotamiton is a mixture of cis and trans isomers. Pharmacokinetics: The pharmacokinetics and systemic absorption of crotamiton following topical application have not been determined. Nonclinical Toxicology Long-term carcinogenicity studies in animals have not been conducted. Clinical Studies Limited information is available regarding clinical studies of crotamiton. How Supplied Eurax is available as: Cream: 60 g tubes Lotion: 60 g (2 oz.) and 454 g (16 oz.) bottles Shake well before use. Storage Store at room temperature. Keep out of reach of children. Alcohol Interaction The interaction between alcohol and crotamiton has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication.
